text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=auth-signing-prod severity=high — multiple 5xx responses from token-verify endpoint (incident id PD-4821).

pagerduty: PD-4821 opened by monitoring-rule ‘auth-signing-error-rate’ — escalation policy: auth-oncall. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-4821

sarah: acked. I’m oncall, jumping in. Any immediate customer impact?

mike: seeing a sharp spike in jwt verify errors in the last 3m. Error: "kid not found" when verifying tokens. Could be a JWKS/key rotation issue.

james: confirming — logs show reject path: `jwt: no matching KID` from verifier and concurrent rotation job ran ~2m before spike. Sample log: 
```
2024-11-08T21:03:12Z auth-verify service=auth node=a12 level=error msg="jwt verify failed" user_id=... err="kid not found: kid=0x7b9f"
```
lia: paging notes — if a key rotation job pushed a new key id before it propagated to all verifiers, we can either roll back rotation or force verifiers to refresh JWKS cache. Quick mitigation: force cache invalidate on verifiers and fallback to previous keys.

sarah: mike/james — steps to invalidate cache safely? I want a one-liner we can run across the fleet.

mike: run this via our orchestration to hit the auth-verify service pods: 
```
# kubectl run -i --tty jwks-refresh --image=appropriate/curl --restart=Never --rm -- 
sh -c "for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=auth-verify -o name); do kubectl exec $p -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/internal/refresh-jwks; done"
```
james: that will trigger a reload. Also safe fallback: temporarily re-enable the old JWKS by updating S3 location pointer (rotation rollback). Lia, can you start the refresh and confirm health?

lia: running the refresh now (kicking off 18 pods). will post progress.

lia: pod auth-verify-1: refresh ok; auth-verify-2: refresh ok; 16/18 done — two still pending, retrying.

sarah: good. mike — if refresh doesn't converge in 5m we roll back. Please prepare rollback steps.

mike: rollback plan ready: set env KEYSET_POINTER=s3://redwood-auth/jwks/v2 and trigger rolling restart of auth-verify. Command: `kubectl set env deployment/auth-verify KEYSET_POINTER=... && kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-verify`

james: note: we should also patch the rotation job to pause for now to avoid flapping. I’ll pause the rotation cron.

pagerduty: PD-4821 acknowledged by sarah at 21:05:03 UTC.

lia: all 18 pods responded to refresh; error rate dropping. Grafana shows failed verify rate down from 6.2% to 0.8% over 4m.

sarah: any known customers still affected? CS reported intermittent auth failures for AcmeCorp and BetaApps. James: can you check request ids and correlate?

james: pulled request traces — most failed requests cluster between 21:02–21:06 and include KID 0x7b9f which is the new key. After refresh, verifiers accept it. Looks like propagation lag to some edge caches.

mike: I also invalidated the CDN edge key cache (edge-cache purge command run). That should fix downstream caches.

lia: monitoring: token verify 5xx count returned to baseline. No new errors in last 2m.

sarah: pausing job rotation and scheduling a follow-up RFC to add canary window to rotations. James, make a postmortem draft and list remediation actions: (1) add staged propagation with canary servers, (2) make refresh endpoint automated post-rotation, (3) alert rule tweak to detect KID mismatch surge earlier.

james: will do. Drafting now.

pagerduty: PD-4821 resolved by sarah at 21:10:60 UTC — incident closed.

sarah: :white_check_mark: closing here. Final customer impact: short-lived auth failures affecting ~3% of traffic for ~4 minutes; no data loss. Follow-up doc and RCA to be shared in #postmortems. Good job team.

incident-bot: Incident PD-4821 closed. Creating ticket for follow-up actions and linking to postmortem workspace.
